reviews.review:
At first, I was sceptical about this entry after Rebellion advertised it as the "big new title," even though it clearly felt more like a standalone DLC for Sniper Elite 5. However, after playing it, I’ve mostly forgiven them because the game feels like a refined version of its predecessor, and it's simply such an awesome franchise.

For a stealth player, the missions are just as engaging as in the last entry. Sniping your way through huge, diverse maps while using sound masking and items is incredibly fun. The excellent Invasion Mode is also back. A great improvement (or feature I appreciate more now) is that campers who stay in one area get punished, which really protects the game experience. A quick tip: avoid invading during working hours. Some players (those sweaty types) clear all enemies beforehand and hide just to farm kills from invaders. So it’s better to play Invasion Mode during evenings or weekends for a fairer experience. The "Propaganda Missions" are probably the biggest addition—they are short but offer cool, specific challenges.

My main complaint would be the AI, which feels frustratingly worse when you compare it with the previous games. Not only do enemies sometimes stay in "suspicious" status forever, but their tactics are sudden and weird, like doing full-sprint across the map. I got spotted so many times because a soldier blindly ran into me head-first before I could even react, which is even worse during an invasion. I’m also not a fan of the Hitman-style assassination objectives; they feel clunky and frustrating when you're trying to stay undetected using specific items. Finally, while story was never the franchise’s strength, the attempt to create a "deep connection" between the side characters and protagonist Harry Hawker felt unnecessary and cringe.

Ultimately, Sniper Elite: Resistance reminded me why I love the mechanics of Sniper Elite 5, even with its flaws. I recommend this to fans of the previous game, newcomers, or even those who weren't convinced about 5 but want to give the formula another shot. I had a great time!
